newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Formosa will drop China project if Taiwan insists.
newsitem.headline: Formosa will drop China project if Taiwan insists.

text.p: Taiwan's Formosa Plastics made clear it would abandon its China power plant project if Taipei holds to its plan to ban firms from investing in utilities and public works there, state radio said on Wednesday.

Formosa chairman Wang Yung-ching reiterated the firm's desire to build the controversial US$3 billion power plant in the mainland's coastal Fujian province, but said the conglomerate would not violate the law.
"Formosa will wait one year for the government's approval," state radio quoted Formosa chairman Wang Yung-ching as saying late on Tuesday.
"If the government still bans such investment after one year, Formosa will give up the project," Wang was quoted as saying.
Wang said in April that Formosa would consider selling its interest to a foreign consortium if Taiwan still had not approved the project in a year's time.

In June 1996, Formosa said it and local Fujian authorities would jointly build a 3,600-megawatt plant, which would be the biggest Taiwan investment in China and the first in the power sector, which Taipei had made off-limits for Taiwan investors.
Taiwan and China have been rivals since a civil war split them in 1949.
Taiwan bans direct investments in China, requiring firms to route even small investments through Hong Kong or other third places after obtaining permits from the economic ministry.
Taiwan still bans investment in major Chinese strategic projects such as power generation and carmaking as well as banking, insurance and other financial projects.
In 1992, Formosa Plastics withdrew a proposal to build a multi-billion dollar petrochemical complex in China -- again under government pressure.--Taipei Newsroom (2-5080815)
